    <div dir='auto' class='story__content  flow-root    pt-1 mt-1 text-4 sm:text-4.5  overflow-visible'><p>Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Saturday assailed the PTI-led Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government over a “lack of governance” in the province.</p>
<p>Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, he alleged that the provincial government was given Rs700 billion under the National Finance Commission for development projects.</p>
<p>“You did not upgrade the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD), did not establish forensic labs, did not install safe city cameras, which should be installed in the merged districts and all the entry-exit points of KP’s districts,” he alleged.</p>
<p>On the other hand, the information minister claimed that the PTI was spending this money on organising protests.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full sm:w-1/2  media--right  media--embed  media--uneven' data-original-src='https://www.dawn.com/news/2036103'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--newskitlink  '>    <iframe
        class="nk-iframe"
        width="100%" frameborder="0" scrolling="no" style="height:250px;position:relative"
        src="https://www.dawn.com/news/card/2036103"
        sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-scripts allow-popups allow-modals allow-forms"></iframe></div>
        
    </figure>
<p>“You don’t even give half an hour to discuss terrorism in the province, but you organise six-hour meetings to spread turmoil and vandalism,” he criticised.</p>
<p>Tarar further said that the PTI had “trapped” millions of people in the province to get its leader, former prime minister Imran Khan, released from jail.</p>
<p>“You trapped them in poverty, in disease by not providing the adequate health facilities, in ignorance by not providing educational opportunities, and in non-development by not improving infrastructure,” he said.</p>
<p>Tarar also alleged that the KP government had held the people of the province “captive to terrorists”.</p>
<p>“From the very first day, this is my opinion that they [PTI] are the B-team of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan,” Tarar said.</p>
<p>The information minister said that the PTI facilitated terrorists in settling in the country.</p>
<p>“For how long will it go on? That the security forces will clear the area of terrorists and establish peace, but you will bring the terrorists back?” he asked.</p>
<p>During his address, Tarar said that the PTI government in KP had dragged the province into the “stone age” during the last 13 and a half years.</p>
<p>Citing various federal government projects, Tarar maintained that there was no comparison of the hours spent working by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to address governance issues and take relief and reform measures.</p>
<p>He said that the chief ministers of all the provinces were working hard, questioning how many hours Afridi spent on governance.</p>
<p>“Tell us if you have ever given a big hospital, a university, a highway to your people, an information technology project to the youth of KP or given them laptops or gadgets,” he said.</p>
<p>“How long can such a system, where there is chaos and extremist politics, continue?” he asked.</p>
<p>He claimed that the KP government wanted to hand over the province to terrorists as it prioritised “personal interests over the national interests”.</p>
<p>“This province needs peace, not politics,” Tarar stated.</p>
<p>Asked about imposing an emergency or governor’s rule in KP, Tarar said that responding to this question would be premature.</p>
<p>“Everyone is asking how long KP and its people will remain at the mercy of its government,” he said.</p>
<p>“In my opinion, the conditions in KP have never been worse. They could not be worse than this. What’s worse than terrorists roaming in the streets? You have designated no-go areas in most of your districts because you collect ransom in collusion with terrorists,” he claimed.</p>
<p>He said that the people of KP go to Punjab or other provinces for medical treatment.</p>
<p>“Will there ever come a time when people from across Pakistan go to KP for treatment?” he asked. The information minister asserted that the PTI would not be allowed to destroy the province.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full  w-full  media--  media--embed  ' data-original-src='https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=im9RwL_b5_Y'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--youtube  '><iframe src='https://www.youtube.com/embed/im9RwL_b5_Y?enablejsapi=1&controls=1&modestbranding=1&rel=0' loading='lazy' allowfullscreen='' frameborder='0' scrolling='no' width='100%' height='100%'></iframe></div>
        
    </figure>
<p>Addressing the same press conference, Coordinator to the Prime Minister on Information for KP Affairs Ikhtiar Wali Khan also questioned the lack of development in the province.</p>
<p>“Universities are shutting down because there are no vice chancellors there. Eighteen out of 34 universities in KP are on the verge of bankruptcy,” he said.</p>
<p>Wali said that people complained about the lack of good roads in Karachi. “But when people of KP go to Karachi, they say that Karachi’s roads are much better than KP.”</p>
<p>Calling on the people and journalists in KP, Wali urged them to talk about the “ground realities”, claiming that the people were crying over the existing health facilities in the province.</p>
<p>He referred to the KP police as the <em>shuhada</em> force, alleging that the provincial government had left them unarmed. He alleged that the PTI government had seized the money allocated to fund the CTD to combat terrorism.</p>
<p>Wali also accused KP ministers of corruption and bad governance in the province.</p>
<p>“The people of KP need peace, health facilities and a political culture based on tolerance, acceptance and respect,” he said.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full sm:w-1/2  media--right  media--embed  media--uneven' data-original-src='https://www.dawn.com/news/2034852'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--newskitlink  '>    <iframe
        class="nk-iframe"
        width="100%" frameborder="0" scrolling="no" style="height:250px;position:relative"
        src="https://www.dawn.com/news/card/2034852"
        sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-scripts allow-popups allow-modals allow-forms"></iframe></div>
        
    </figure>
<p>The PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre — have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy. This was also a <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2034693/naqvi-says-talks-with-opposition-have-collapsed-accuses-kp-cm-of-sabotaging-negotiations">key reason</a> behind the <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2034734/pti-terms-access-to-imran-principal-point-of-deadlock-claims-centre-refused-to-include-it-in-agreement">breakdown</a> of the <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2034465/after-hours-of-negotiations-second-round-of-govt-opposition-talks-ends-in-a-deadlock">Oct 3 talks</a> between them.</p>
<p>The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2035383#:~:text=being%20left%20out%20of%20decisions%20concerning%20the%20Centre%E2%80%99s%20counterterrorism%20policy%20was%20%E2%80%9Ccompletely%20wrong%E2%80%9D%20and%20%E2%80%9Cmisleading">denied</a>. It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2033266">criticises</a> the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2032947">stance</a> on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.</p>
<h2><a id="kundi-muqam-discuss-kps-security-and-political-situation" href="#kundi-muqam-discuss-kps-security-and-political-situation" class="heading-permalink" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" title="Permalink"></a>Kundi, Muqam discuss KP’s security and political situation</h2>
<p>In Peshawar, Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit Baltistan Amir Muqam met KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi at Governor House, where they discussed the overall law and order situation in the province.</p>
<p>According to a joint statement issued after the meeting, the two leaders also discussed the PTI’s long march and exchanged views on issues of mutual interest, particularly the political environment in the province.</p>
<p>Kundi and Muqam thanked the people of KP, saying they had rejected the politics of unrest and confrontation.</p>
<p>They reiterated that the federal government would continue taking all possible measures to restore lasting peace, strengthen security and accelerate public welfare and development in the province.</p>
<p>The two leaders also observed that the people of KP had grown frustrated with terrorism and what they described as political elements promoting instability, reaffirming the federal government’s commitment to ensuring peace and stability in the province.</p>
<p>In a post on X, Kundi said, “Our people have paid an unbearable price in the war against terrorism. They cannot be held hostage to the politics of anarchy and agitation.”</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full  w-full  media--  media--embed  media--uneven media--tweet' data-original-src='https://x.com/fkkundi/status/2108863697842282696'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--twitter  '><span>
    <blockquote class="twitter-tweet" lang="en">
        <a href="https://twitter.com/fkkundi/status/2108863697842282696"></a>
    </blockquote>
</span></div>
        
    </figure>
<p>He affirmed that the federal government “will continue to take all possible measures to strengthen security, protect our people and support the province’s development”.</p>
<p>“The future of KP cannot be sacrificed at the altar of political ambition,” the governor declared.</p>
<p>“This province does not need any more political stunts that undermine security and endanger lives. I commend the people of KP for standing with peace,” he wrote.</p>
<p>In recent days, federal ministers have assailed the PTI for staging a <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2035927/dare-and-cross-swabi-kundi-challenges-pti-long-march-participants">protest long march</a>, which it has been <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2031568">warned</a> against, at a time when KP faces security challenges. They have also linked differences over the counterterrorism policy with the <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2035457">possibility</a> of an emergency or governor’s rule in KP.</p>
<p>On Friday, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2035966">Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said</a> the government had finished deliberating on the imposition of an emergency and warned that it would avail the option if the KP government did not cooperate on counterterrorism.</p>
<h2><a id="gohar-meets-cm-afridi" href="#gohar-meets-cm-afridi" class="heading-permalink" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" title="Permalink"></a>Gohar meets CM Afridi</h2>
<p>On the other hand, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said on X that he met CM Afridi in Peshawar to discuss the country’s political situation, the party’s long march and “other important matters”.</p>
<p>PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, MNA Junaid Akbar, Parliamentary Leader Shahid Kattak and KP Information Minister Shafi Jani were also present during the meeting.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full  w-full  media--  media--embed  media--uneven media--tweet' data-original-src='https://x.com/BarristerGohar/status/2108873111664030190'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--twitter  '><span>
    <blockquote class="twitter-tweet" lang="en">
        <a href="https://twitter.com/BarristerGohar/status/2108873111664030190"></a>
    </blockquote>
</span></div>
        
    </figure>
<p>Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Gohar said the imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency was not the right solution to the province’s issues, considering the “circumstances”.</p>
<p>The PTI chairman said there were no conflicting views on eradicating terrorism, but rather on the method of doing so, which could be resolved.</p>
<p>“Those who have taken up swords against the state [and[ those who are enemies of the state are our enemies; if they can be eradicated by imposing governor’s rule or an emergency, we would welcome it, but this would further deteriorate the situation,” Gohar said.</p>
<p>He called on the country’s political leadership to “demonstrate political wisdom” and said a meeting of either the federal or provincial apex committee should be called if any situation required the imposition of governor’s rule.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full  w-full  media--  media--embed  media--uneven media--tweet' data-original-src='https://x.com/BarristerGohar/status/2108900023379570885'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--twitter  '><span>
    <blockquote class="twitter-tweet" lang="en">
        <a href="https://twitter.com/BarristerGohar/status/2108900023379570885"></a>
    </blockquote>
</span></div>
        
    </figure>
<h2><a id="pti-rejects-allegations-linking-it-to-terrorists" href="#pti-rejects-allegations-linking-it-to-terrorists" class="heading-permalink" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" title="Permalink"></a>PTI rejects allegations linking it to terrorists</h2>
<p>In a statement issued later in the day, PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram responded to the “outbursts of the so-called ministers and political orphans”.</p>
<p>He rejected allegations linking PTI to armed groups, declaring that the party neither supported armed struggle nor believed in the politics of violence and sabotage.</p>
<p>He said that “daily press conferences by liar-brigade, attacking PTI, were diverting attention from Pakistan’s economic, social and security challenges, lamenting that such useless and harmful pressers consumed valuable media airtime that could otherwise be used for public education, awareness programmes and substantive discussions on issues affecting ordinary citizens”.</p>
<p>The PTI leader challenged the federal government to prove the effectiveness of its security and administrative policies first in Balochistan, where, he claimed, large areas had become no-go zones, before replicating the failed policies elsewhere in the country.</p>
<p>Otherwise, he urged, the government should accept the comprehensive plan unanimously approved by the KP Grand Jirga peace plan to eradicate terrorism once and for all.</p>
<p>He further called for a comprehensive counterterrorism strategy “combining effective security operations with meaningful political engagement and respect for the rights of local communities”.</p>
<p>Referring to the Oct 3 talks with the government, the PTI leader claimed terrorism had not initially been central to the dialogue agenda but was subsequently introduced by the government, shifting attention away from other outstanding political issues.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full sm:w-1/2  media--right  media--embed  media--uneven' data-original-src='https://www.dawn.com/news/2034734'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--newskitlink  '>    <iframe
        class="nk-iframe"
        width="100%" frameborder="0" scrolling="no" style="height:250px;position:relative"
        src="https://www.dawn.com/news/card/2034734"
        sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-scripts allow-popups allow-modals allow-forms"></iframe></div>
        
    </figure>
<p>Akram questioned the effectiveness of the government’s counterterrorism strategy, contending that policies “relying on force while overlooking local grievances had repeatedly caused destruction, displacement and resentment”.</p>
<p>According to the statement, the PTI leader acknowledged that KP faced security challenges but rejected claims that 11 districts had become no-go areas, calling such assertions “exaggerated and a possible pretext for imposing emergency measures or undermining the provincial government”.</p>
<p>The information secretary maintained that the Centre must respect the “mandate of KP’s elected government and refrain from interfering in provincial affairs”.</p>
<p>He vowed that PTI would “resist any attempt to impose decisions or legislation that compromised the constitutional rights of residents of the province and its merged districts”.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full  w-full  media--  media--embed  media--uneven media--tweet' data-original-src='https://x.com/PTIofficial/status/2108910924065361932'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--twitter  '><span>
    <blockquote class="twitter-tweet" lang="en">
        <a href="https://twitter.com/PTIofficial/status/2108910924065361932"></a>
    </blockquote>
</span></div>
        
    </figure>

    </div>

        <div class='media__item    media__item--100          '><a title="Afridi invites people from across country to join PTI's long march at Swabi Interchange on Oct 11" href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2035927/afridi-invites-people-from-across-country-to-join-ptis-long-march-at-swabi-interchange-on-oct-11" target="_self"><picture><img class='lazyload' src='data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAEAAAABCAQAAAC1HAwCAAAAC0lEQVR42mN8Vw8AAmEBb87E6jIAAAAASUVORK5CYII=' data-src="https://i.dawn.com/medium/2026/10/0923495540e89b8.webp" data-srcset='https://i.dawn.com/thumbnail/2026/10/0923495540e89b8.webp 300w, https://i.dawn.com/medium/2026/10/0923495540e89b8.webp 500w, https://i.dawn.com/large/2026/10/0923495540e89b8.webp 800w' alt="Afridi invites people from across country to join PTI's long march at Swabi Interchange on Oct 11" title="Afridi invites people from across country to join PTI's long march at Swabi Interchange on Oct 11"  /></picture></a></div>

headline: Govt assails PTI over 'lack of governance' in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
description: Attaullah Tarar says PTI has dragged KP into "stone age"; PTI rejects allegations linking it to terrorist groups; Muqam meets Kundi; Gohar calls on KP CM and says emergency not the "solution".
author: News Desk
article_text:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Saturday assailed the PTI-led Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government over a “lack of governance” in the province.

Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, he alleged that the provincial government was given Rs700 billion under the National Finance Commission for development projects.

“You did not upgrade the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD), did not establish forensic labs, did not install safe city cameras, which should be installed in the merged districts and all the entry-exit points of KP’s districts,” he alleged.

On the other hand, the information minister claimed that the PTI was spending this money on organising protests.

“You don’t even give half an hour to discuss terrorism in the province, but you organise six-hour meetings to spread turmoil and vandalism,” he criticised.

Tarar further said that the PTI had “trapped” millions of people in the province to get its leader, former prime minister Imran Khan, released from jail.

“You trapped them in poverty, in disease by not providing the adequate health facilities, in ignorance by not providing educational opportunities, and in non-development by not improving infrastructure,” he said.

Tarar also alleged that the KP government had held the people of the province “captive to terrorists”.

“From the very first day, this is my opinion that they [PTI] are the B-team of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan,” Tarar said.

The information minister said that the PTI facilitated terrorists in settling in the country.

“For how long will it go on? That the security forces will clear the area of terrorists and establish peace, but you will bring the terrorists back?” he asked.

During his address, Tarar said that the PTI government in KP had dragged the province into the “stone age” during the last 13 and a half years.

Citing various federal government projects, Tarar maintained that there was no comparison of the hours spent working by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to address governance issues and take relief and reform measures.

He said that the chief ministers of all the provinces were working hard, questioning how many hours Afridi spent on governance.

“Tell us if you have ever given a big hospital, a university, a highway to your people, an information technology project to the youth of KP or given them laptops or gadgets,” he said.

“How long can such a system, where there is chaos and extremist politics, continue?” he asked.

He claimed that the KP government wanted to hand over the province to terrorists as it prioritised “personal interests over the national interests”.

“This province needs peace, not politics,” Tarar stated.

Asked about imposing an emergency or governor’s rule in KP, Tarar said that responding to this question would be premature.

“Everyone is asking how long KP and its people will remain at the mercy of its government,” he said.

“In my opinion, the conditions in KP have never been worse. They could not be worse than this. What’s worse than terrorists roaming in the streets? You have designated no-go areas in most of your districts because you collect ransom in collusion with terrorists,” he claimed.

He said that the people of KP go to Punjab or other provinces for medical treatment.

“Will there ever come a time when people from across Pakistan go to KP for treatment?” he asked. The information minister asserted that the PTI would not be allowed to destroy the province.

Addressing the same press conference, Coordinator to the Prime Minister on Information for KP Affairs Ikhtiar Wali Khan also questioned the lack of development in the province.

“Universities are shutting down because there are no vice chancellors there. Eighteen out of 34 universities in KP are on the verge of bankruptcy,” he said.

Wali said that people complained about the lack of good roads in Karachi. “But when people of KP go to Karachi, they say that Karachi’s roads are much better than KP.”

Calling on the people and journalists in KP, Wali urged them to talk about the “ground realities”, claiming that the people were crying over the existing health facilities in the province.

He referred to the KP police as the shuhada force, alleging that the provincial government had left them unarmed. He alleged that the PTI government had seized the money allocated to fund the CTD to combat terrorism.

Wali also accused KP ministers of corruption and bad governance in the province.

“The people of KP need peace, health facilities and a political culture based on tolerance, acceptance and respect,” he said.

The PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre — have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy. This was also a key reason behind the breakdown of the Oct 3 talks between them.

The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied. It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticises the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

Kundi, Muqam discuss KP’s security and political situation

In Peshawar, Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit Baltistan Amir Muqam met KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi at Governor House, where they discussed the overall law and order situation in the province.

According to a joint statement issued after the meeting, the two leaders also discussed the PTI’s long march and exchanged views on issues of mutual interest, particularly the political environment in the province.

Kundi and Muqam thanked the people of KP, saying they had rejected the politics of unrest and confrontation.

They reiterated that the federal government would continue taking all possible measures to restore lasting peace, strengthen security and accelerate public welfare and development in the province.

The two leaders also observed that the people of KP had grown frustrated with terrorism and what they described as political elements promoting instability, reaffirming the federal government’s commitment to ensuring peace and stability in the province.

In a post on X, Kundi said, “Our people have paid an unbearable price in the war against terrorism. They cannot be held hostage to the politics of anarchy and agitation.”

He affirmed that the federal government “will continue to take all possible measures to strengthen security, protect our people and support the province’s development”.

“The future of KP cannot be sacrificed at the altar of political ambition,” the governor declared.

“This province does not need any more political stunts that undermine security and endanger lives. I commend the people of KP for standing with peace,” he wrote.

In recent days, federal ministers have assailed the PTI for staging a protest long march, which it has been warned against, at a time when KP faces security challenges. They have also linked differences over the counterterrorism policy with the possibility of an emergency or governor’s rule in KP.

On Friday, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the government had finished deliberating on the imposition of an emergency and warned that it would avail the option if the KP government did not cooperate on counterterrorism.

Gohar meets CM Afridi

On the other hand, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said on X that he met CM Afridi in Peshawar to discuss the country’s political situation, the party’s long march and “other important matters”.

PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, MNA Junaid Akbar, Parliamentary Leader Shahid Kattak and KP Information Minister Shafi Jani were also present during the meeting.

Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Gohar said the imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency was not the right solution to the province’s issues, considering the “circumstances”.

The PTI chairman said there were no conflicting views on eradicating terrorism, but rather on the method of doing so, which could be resolved.

“Those who have taken up swords against the state [and[ those who are enemies of the state are our enemies; if they can be eradicated by imposing governor’s rule or an emergency, we would welcome it, but this would further deteriorate the situation,” Gohar said.

He called on the country’s political leadership to “demonstrate political wisdom” and said a meeting of either the federal or provincial apex committee should be called if any situation required the imposition of governor’s rule.

PTI rejects allegations linking it to terrorists

In a statement issued later in the day, PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram responded to the “outbursts of the so-called ministers and political orphans”.

He rejected allegations linking PTI to armed groups, declaring that the party neither supported armed struggle nor believed in the politics of violence and sabotage.

He said that “daily press conferences by liar-brigade, attacking PTI, were diverting attention from Pakistan’s economic, social and security challenges, lamenting that such useless and harmful pressers consumed valuable media airtime that could otherwise be used for public education, awareness programmes and substantive discussions on issues affecting ordinary citizens”.

The PTI leader challenged the federal government to prove the effectiveness of its security and administrative policies first in Balochistan, where, he claimed, large areas had become no-go zones, before replicating the failed policies elsewhere in the country.

Otherwise, he urged, the government should accept the comprehensive plan unanimously approved by the KP Grand Jirga peace plan to eradicate terrorism once and for all.

He further called for a comprehensive counterterrorism strategy “combining effective security operations with meaningful political engagement and respect for the rights of local communities”.

Referring to the Oct 3 talks with the government, the PTI leader claimed terrorism had not initially been central to the dialogue agenda but was subsequently introduced by the government, shifting attention away from other outstanding political issues.

Akram questioned the effectiveness of the government’s counterterrorism strategy, contending that policies “relying on force while overlooking local grievances had repeatedly caused destruction, displacement and resentment”.

According to the statement, the PTI leader acknowledged that KP faced security challenges but rejected claims that 11 districts had become no-go areas, calling such assertions “exaggerated and a possible pretext for imposing emergency measures or undermining the provincial government”.

The information secretary maintained that the Centre must respect the “mandate of KP’s elected government and refrain from interfering in provincial affairs”.

He vowed that PTI would “resist any attempt to impose decisions or legislation that compromised the constitutional rights of residents of the province and its merged districts”.

article_html:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar on Saturday assailed the PTI-led Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government over a “lack of governance” in the province.

Addressing a press conference in Islamabad, he alleged that the provincial government was given Rs700 billion under the National Finance Commission for development projects.

“You did not upgrade the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD), did not establish forensic labs, did not install safe city cameras, which should be installed in the merged districts and all the entry-exit points of KP’s districts,” he alleged.

On the other hand, the information minister claimed that the PTI was spending this money on organising protests.

“You don’t even give half an hour to discuss terrorism in the province, but you organise six-hour meetings to spread turmoil and vandalism,” he criticised.

Tarar further said that the PTI had “trapped” millions of people in the province to get its leader, former prime minister Imran Khan, released from jail.

“You trapped them in poverty, in disease by not providing the adequate health facilities, in ignorance by not providing educational opportunities, and in non-development by not improving infrastructure,” he said.

Tarar also alleged that the KP government had held the people of the province “captive to terrorists”.

“From the very first day, this is my opinion that they [PTI] are the B-team of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan,” Tarar said.

The information minister said that the PTI facilitated terrorists in settling in the country.

“For how long will it go on? That the security forces will clear the area of terrorists and establish peace, but you will bring the terrorists back?” he asked.

During his address, Tarar said that the PTI government in KP had dragged the province into the “stone age” during the last 13 and a half years.

Citing various federal government projects, Tarar maintained that there was no comparison of the hours spent working by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to address governance issues and take relief and reform measures.

He said that the chief ministers of all the provinces were working hard, questioning how many hours Afridi spent on governance.

“Tell us if you have ever given a big hospital, a university, a highway to your people, an information technology project to the youth of KP or given them laptops or gadgets,” he said.

“How long can such a system, where there is chaos and extremist politics, continue?” he asked.

He claimed that the KP government wanted to hand over the province to terrorists as it prioritised “personal interests over the national interests”.

“This province needs peace, not politics,” Tarar stated.

Asked about imposing an emergency or governor’s rule in KP, Tarar said that responding to this question would be premature.

“Everyone is asking how long KP and its people will remain at the mercy of its government,” he said.

“In my opinion, the conditions in KP have never been worse. They could not be worse than this. What’s worse than terrorists roaming in the streets? You have designated no-go areas in most of your districts because you collect ransom in collusion with terrorists,” he claimed.

He said that the people of KP go to Punjab or other provinces for medical treatment.

“Will there ever come a time when people from across Pakistan go to KP for treatment?” he asked. The information minister asserted that the PTI would not be allowed to destroy the province.

Addressing the same press conference, Coordinator to the Prime Minister on Information for KP Affairs Ikhtiar Wali Khan also questioned the lack of development in the province.

“Universities are shutting down because there are no vice chancellors there. Eighteen out of 34 universities in KP are on the verge of bankruptcy,” he said.

Wali said that people complained about the lack of good roads in Karachi. “But when people of KP go to Karachi, they say that Karachi’s roads are much better than KP.”

Calling on the people and journalists in KP, Wali urged them to talk about the “ground realities”, claiming that the people were crying over the existing health facilities in the province.

He referred to the KP police as the shuhada force, alleging that the provincial government had left them unarmed. He alleged that the PTI government had seized the money allocated to fund the CTD to combat terrorism.

Wali also accused KP ministers of corruption and bad governance in the province.

“The people of KP need peace, health facilities and a political culture based on tolerance, acceptance and respect,” he said.

The PML-N-led federal government and the KP government led by PTI — which is in opposition in the Centre — have been at odds over various issues, particularly on the counterterrorism policy. This was also a key reason behind the breakdown of the Oct 3 talks between them.

The PTI has said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre has denied. It also calls for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticises the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objects to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban.

Kundi, Muqam discuss KP’s security and political situation

In Peshawar, Minister for Kashmir Affairs and Gilgit Baltistan Amir Muqam met KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi at Governor House, where they discussed the overall law and order situation in the province.

According to a joint statement issued after the meeting, the two leaders also discussed the PTI’s long march and exchanged views on issues of mutual interest, particularly the political environment in the province.

Kundi and Muqam thanked the people of KP, saying they had rejected the politics of unrest and confrontation.

They reiterated that the federal government would continue taking all possible measures to restore lasting peace, strengthen security and accelerate public welfare and development in the province.

The two leaders also observed that the people of KP had grown frustrated with terrorism and what they described as political elements promoting instability, reaffirming the federal government’s commitment to ensuring peace and stability in the province.

In a post on X, Kundi said, “Our people have paid an unbearable price in the war against terrorism. They cannot be held hostage to the politics of anarchy and agitation.”

He affirmed that the federal government “will continue to take all possible measures to strengthen security, protect our people and support the province’s development”.

“The future of KP cannot be sacrificed at the altar of political ambition,” the governor declared.

“This province does not need any more political stunts that undermine security and endanger lives. I commend the people of KP for standing with peace,” he wrote.

In recent days, federal ministers have assailed the PTI for staging a protest long march, which it has been warned against, at a time when KP faces security challenges. They have also linked differences over the counterterrorism policy with the possibility of an emergency or governor’s rule in KP.

On Friday, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the government had finished deliberating on the imposition of an emergency and warned that it would avail the option if the KP government did not cooperate on counterterrorism.

Gohar meets CM Afridi

On the other hand, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said on X that he met CM Afridi in Peshawar to discuss the country’s political situation, the party’s long march and “other important matters”.

PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, MNA Junaid Akbar, Parliamentary Leader Shahid Kattak and KP Information Minister Shafi Jani were also present during the meeting.

Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Gohar said the imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency was not the right solution to the province’s issues, considering the “circumstances”.

The PTI chairman said there were no conflicting views on eradicating terrorism, but rather on the method of doing so, which could be resolved.

“Those who have taken up swords against the state [and[ those who are enemies of the state are our enemies; if they can be eradicated by imposing governor’s rule or an emergency, we would welcome it, but this would further deteriorate the situation,” Gohar said.

He called on the country’s political leadership to “demonstrate political wisdom” and said a meeting of either the federal or provincial apex committee should be called if any situation required the imposition of governor’s rule.

PTI rejects allegations linking it to terrorists

In a statement issued later in the day, PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram responded to the “outbursts of the so-called ministers and political orphans”.

He rejected allegations linking PTI to armed groups, declaring that the party neither supported armed struggle nor believed in the politics of violence and sabotage.

He said that “daily press conferences by liar-brigade, attacking PTI, were diverting attention from Pakistan’s economic, social and security challenges, lamenting that such useless and harmful pressers consumed valuable media airtime that could otherwise be used for public education, awareness programmes and substantive discussions on issues affecting ordinary citizens”.

The PTI leader challenged the federal government to prove the effectiveness of its security and administrative policies first in Balochistan, where, he claimed, large areas had become no-go zones, before replicating the failed policies elsewhere in the country.

Otherwise, he urged, the government should accept the comprehensive plan unanimously approved by the KP Grand Jirga peace plan to eradicate terrorism once and for all.

He further called for a comprehensive counterterrorism strategy “combining effective security operations with meaningful political engagement and respect for the rights of local communities”.

Referring to the Oct 3 talks with the government, the PTI leader claimed terrorism had not initially been central to the dialogue agenda but was subsequently introduced by the government, shifting attention away from other outstanding political issues.

Akram questioned the effectiveness of the government’s counterterrorism strategy, contending that policies “relying on force while overlooking local grievances had repeatedly caused destruction, displacement and resentment”.

According to the statement, the PTI leader acknowledged that KP faced security challenges but rejected claims that 11 districts had become no-go areas, calling such assertions “exaggerated and a possible pretext for imposing emergency measures or undermining the provincial government”.

The information secretary maintained that the Centre must respect the “mandate of KP’s elected government and refrain from interfering in provincial affairs”.

He vowed that PTI would “resist any attempt to impose decisions or legislation that compromised the constitutional rights of residents of the province and its merged districts”.

    <!-- box/content -->
    <div dir='auto' class='story__content  flow-root    pt-1 mt-1 text-4 sm:text-4.5  overflow-visible'><p>QUETTA: Ten terrorists were killed in a targeted intelligence-based operation conducted by the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) in Balochistan’s Barkhan district, the Home Department said on Saturday.</p>
<p>An aide in the Home Department, Babar Yousafzai, said: “During an intense gun battle, 10 armed terrorists were killed and two CTD officials were injured.”</p>
<p>The CTD had conducted a targeted operation after receiving credible information about the presence of terrorists belonging to the Indian proxy, <em>Fitna al Hindustan</em>, in the area, according to Yousafzai.</p>
<p>The state has <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/1914525"><u>designated</u></a> Balochistan-based terrorist groups as <em>Fitna-al-Hindustan</em> to <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/1912930#:~:text=The%20term%20%E2%80%98Fitna%20al%20Hindu%C2%ADstan%E2%80%99%20is%20a%20new%20phrase%20coined%20by%20Pakistan%E2%80%99s%20military%2C%20aimed%20at%20framing%20India%E2%80%99s%20alleged%20role%20in%20terrorism%20as%20a%20deliberate%20destabilisation%20strategy%2C%20potentially%20to%20galvanise%20domestic%20support."><u>highlight</u></a> India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.</p>
<p>Yousafzai added that the CTD had also seized a large quantity of arms, ammunition and explosives from the terrorists.</p>
<p>According to other officials in the department, two CTD personnel were taken to a hospital, while the bodies of the terrorists were taken to the Rara Sham district hospital.</p>
<p>Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti paid rich tributes to the personnel of CTD for conducting the successful operation.</p>
<p>He said that our brave security forces were playing an important role in the elimination of terrorism from Balochistan and rendering sacrifices to protect the lives and property of the people.</p>
<p>On Oct 7, security forces <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2035365">killed</a> five terrorists belonging to <em>Fitna al-Hindustan i</em>n Balochistan’s Mastung district, according to state media.</p>
<p>Late last month, the military’s media affairs wing said that more than 71 terrorists had been <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2033043"><u>killed</u></a> in Shaban and other areas of Balochistan during 96 hours.</p>
<p>On Sept 17, three terrorists were <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2030608"><u>eliminated</u></a> in an IBO in Balochistan’s Awaran district’s Badrang area. Another three were <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2029834"><u>killed</u></a> in Mastung on Sept 14. Earlier that month, 21 terrorists were <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2026635"><u>killed</u></a> in separate engagements in Nokcha, Chagai, Ziarat Cross, and Pishin.</p>
<p>The number of terrorist attacks in the province increased by seven per cent from 83 in July to 89 in August, according to PICSS’ <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2026645"><u>monthly assessment</u></a>. As per the report, Balochistan was declared the province “most affected” by terrorism.</p>

headline: 10 terrorists killed during CTD operation in Barkhan, says Balochistan govt
description: Home Dept aide says two CTD officials injured; arms, ammunition seized from terrorists.
author: Saleem Shahid
article_text:
QUETTA: Ten terrorists were killed in a targeted intelligence-based operation conducted by the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) in Balochistan’s Barkhan district, the Home Department said on Saturday.

An aide in the Home Department, Babar Yousafzai, said: “During an intense gun battle, 10 armed terrorists were killed and two CTD officials were injured.”

The CTD had conducted a targeted operation after receiving credible information about the presence of terrorists belonging to the Indian proxy, Fitna al Hindustan, in the area, according to Yousafzai.

The state has designated Balochistan-based terrorist groups as Fitna-al-Hindustan to highlight India’s alleged role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

Yousafzai added that the CTD had also seized a large quantity of arms, ammunition and explosives from the terrorists.

According to other officials in the department, two CTD personnel were taken to a hospital, while the bodies of the terrorists were taken to the Rara Sham district hospital.

Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti paid rich tributes to the personnel of CTD for conducting the successful operation.

He said that our brave security forces were playing an important role in the elimination of terrorism from Balochistan and rendering sacrifices to protect the lives and property of the people.

On Oct 7, security forces killed five terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Hindustan in Balochistan’s Mastung district, according to state media.

Late last month, the military’s media affairs wing said that more than 71 terrorists had been killed in Shaban and other areas of Balochistan during 96 hours.

On Sept 17, three terrorists were eliminated in an IBO in Balochistan’s Awaran district’s Badrang area. Another three were killed in Mastung on Sept 14. Earlier that month, 21 terrorists were killed in separate engagements in Nokcha, Chagai, Ziarat Cross, and Pishin.

The number of terrorist attacks in the province increased by seven per cent from 83 in July to 89 in August, according to PICSS’ monthly assessment. As per the report, Balochistan was declared the province “most affected” by terrorism.

    <div dir='auto' class='story__content  flow-root    pt-1 mt-1 text-4 sm:text-4.5  overflow-visible'><p>CHARSADDA/MARDAN: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Saturday said he will not accept any “illegal move”, including the imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency.</p>
<p>The KP CM made the remarks while addressing his supporters in Mardan, where the PTI long march led by him arrived on its seventh day. The federal government, citing differences over the counterterrorism policy, is <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2036160/pm-shehbaz-meets-president-zardari-as-centre-mulls-imposition-of-emergency-in-kp">mulling the option</a> of imposing an emergency or governor’s rule in KP.</p>
<p>Afridi said that if governor’s rule was imposed or any “wrong decision” was taken, the long march would head to Peshawar instead of Swabi, and then move towards D-Chowk in Islamabad.</p>
<p>He urged the public to come out for the release of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, adding that Pakhtuns would not be intimidated by threats, guns or bullets.</p>
<p>The KP CM asserted that arrests and other measures could not demoralise PTI workers. He said that his party would continue its struggle to end the injustices being committed against Imran and secure his release.</p>
<p>Speaking on the occasion, MNA Muhammad Atif Khan contended that Afridi had placed the federal government in a difficult position through his strategy.</p>

</span></div>
        
    </figure>
<p>The PTI launched the march despite warnings from the Centre after Oct 3 <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2034465/after-hours-of-negotiations-second-round-of-govt-opposition-talks-ends-in-a-deadlock"><u>talks</u></a> with the federal government <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2034693/naqvi-says-talks-with-opposition-have-collapsed-accuses-kp-cm-of-sabotaging-negotiations"><u>failed</u></a> to bridge their differences for <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2034734/pti-terms-access-to-imran-principal-point-of-deadlock-claims-centre-refused-to-include-it-in-agreement"><u>multiple reasons</u></a>, particularly over counterterrorism measures.</p>
<p>The route plan for the march has undergone multiple changes since its <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2034698/we-are-not-yes-men-cm-afridi-launches-pti-long-march-to-islamabad-from-lakki-marwat">launch</a> on Oct 4. While the party initially <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2032588"><u>vowed</u></a> to march towards Islamabad, its final destination seemingly remains <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2035434#:~:text=told%20Dawn%20that%20the%20final%20destination%20remained%20tentative%20for%20now"><u>tentative</u></a> as the KP CM has yet to announce the plan for the trek after Oct 11, <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2036087">beyond Swabi</a>.</p>
<p>So far, the march — being carried out to demand Imran’s release — has remained within KP, where the PTI is in power.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full  w-full  media--  media--embed  media--uneven media--tweet' data-original-src='https://x.com/ShafiJanPTI/status/2108855650503872967'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--twitter  '><span>
    <blockquote class="twitter-tweet" lang="en">
        <a href="https://twitter.com/ShafiJanPTI/status/2108855650503872967"></a>
    </blockquote>
</span></div>
        
    </figure>
<h2><a id="swabi-authorities-prepare-for-pti-march" href="#swabi-authorities-prepare-for-pti-march" class="heading-permalink" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" title="Permalink"></a>Swabi authorities prepare for PTI march</h2>
<p>Meanwhile, containers have been transported to Swabi Interchange and the Indus River bridge on the M-1 Motorway to block the party’s march, but the motorway and the Grand Trunk Road remain open to traffic.</p>
<p>The bridge is particularly significant because it links Punjab and KP, which lie on opposite banks of the river.</p>
<p>Afridi earlier <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2035927">called on PTI supporters</a> across Pakistan to reach the Swabi Interchange on Oct 11 to join his long march.</p>
<p>However, PTI district president Sohail Yousafzai said the convoy would reach Swabi on Oct 12 (Monday), adding that Afridi had directed party workers, lawmakers and office-bearers from across the country to reach Swabi by then.</p>
<p>Echoing a plan announced by Afridi earlier, Yousafzai said that convoys from the Peshawar, Malakand and Kohat regions would reach Swabi Interchange on Oct 13, while those from Hazara, Bannu and Dera Ismail Khan would arrive the next day, when the CM Afridi would announce the next course of action.</p>
<p>The KP chief executive is expected to address party workers at Shewa Adda in Razaar tehsil at 1pm, at the district headquarters at 3pm and at Topi tehsil at 5pm, which shares a boundary with Ghazi in Haripur district.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full  w-full  media--  media--embed  media--uneven media--tweet' data-original-src='https://x.com/ShafiJanPTI/status/2108789823440044146'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--twitter  '><span>
    <blockquote class="twitter-tweet" lang="en">
        <a href="https://twitter.com/ShafiJanPTI/status/2108789823440044146"></a>
    </blockquote>
</span></div>
        
    </figure>
<p>In a post on X earlier in the day, KP Information Minister Shafi Jan said the convoy will stay overnight in Mardan. He also said the future course of action will be announced on Oct 13 and they will move beyond Swabi.</p>
<h2><a id="refused-pressure-afridi-claims" href="#refused-pressure-afridi-claims" class="heading-permalink" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" title="Permalink"></a>Refused pressure, Afridi claims</h2>
<p>Earlier in the day, the KP CM addressed a large gathering at Farooq-i-Azam Chowk in Charsadda, where he reiterated his opposition to any military operations in the province.</p>
<p>Afridi said he stood firmly with the people and would not accept decisions imposed through pressure or threats.</p>
<p>“I was asked to sign, but I refused,” he said, adding that he would neither retreat from his position under pressure nor compromise on his principles.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full sm:w-1/2  media--right  media--embed  media--uneven' data-original-src='https://www.dawn.com/news/2034852/situationer-can-afridi-strike-a-balance-between-agitation-governance'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--newskitlink  '>    <iframe
        class="nk-iframe"
        width="100%" frameborder="0" scrolling="no" style="height:250px;position:relative"
        src="https://www.dawn.com/news/card/2034852"
        sandbox="allow-same-origin allow-scripts allow-popups allow-modals allow-forms"></iframe></div>
        
    </figure>
<p>Afridi said his position on national security and the Kashmir issue was clear and unequivocal. He noted that important national matters should be addressed on the basis of principles rather than political pressure.</p>
<p>Referring to what he alleged were preparations for a possible military operation, the KP CM reiterated that he would not sign any document under pressure. He claimed attempts had been made to persuade him to agree to certain decisions, but he had declined.</p>
<p>Afridi has <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2031201"><u>repeatedly</u></a> voiced his <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/1954721"><u>opposition</u></a> to the federal government’s policies on counterterrorism and Afghanistan since he was elected as the KP chief minister in October 2025.</p>
<p>Speaking in Charsadda, the PTI leader stressed the need to protect public rights, democratic values and the people’s mandate, saying public aspirations and ground realities should not be ignored in decision-making. He urged party workers to remain united and maintain discipline in their political struggle.</p>
<p>He <a rel="nofollow noopener noreferrer" target="_blank" class="link--external" href="https://x.com/PTIofficial/status/2108915316482867367">referred</a> to the “threats” of the imposition of governor’s rule or emergency, adding that the matter “had gone beyond seats and power” and he was ready to “sacrifice” his seat for Imran and Pakhtuns.</p>
<p>The chief minister highlighted that KP had suffered immense losses in the fight against terrorism, adding that the sacrifices made by its residents should not be forgotten and that their concerns regarding peace, stability and fundamental rights deserved serious attention.</p>
<p>Afridi reiterated he would announce the next plan of action on Oct 13 at the Swabi interchange.</p>
<p>He called on PTI workers to remain united in their struggle for their rights, adding that political differences should be resolved through democratic means and that the voice of the people should be respected.</p>
<p>The KP CM urged party supporters to remain steadfast and vigilant amid the prevailing political situation.</p>
<p>The gathering drew hundreds of PTI supporters to the roundabout, many wearing red caps and chanting slogans in support of Imran. The chief minister addressed the crowd from a container alongside party leaders.</p>
<h2><a id="guidelines-issued-for-police-to-deal-with-protests" href="#guidelines-issued-for-police-to-deal-with-protests" class="heading-permalink" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1" title="Permalink"></a>Guidelines issued for police to deal with protests</h2>
<p>While the PTI seemed determined to continue with its long march, KP Inspector General Zulfiqar Hameed issued operational guidelines to the police to deal with protests.</p>
<p>The document issued by the police chief, available with <em>Dawn</em>, noted that in “all cases of public protests there is a possibility that miscreants and anti-state elements may use an opportunity to [incite] violence and carry out sabotage activities”.</p>
<p>To prevent such acts, the guidelines were issued in continuation of Operational Guidelines-9/2013 and in light of Sections 83 to 88 of the KP Police Act 2017, for “strict compliance”.</p>
<p>The KP IG directed personnel to exercise “maximum restraint” and avoid the use of force for peaceful protests. “The protesters shall be engaged in negotiations through the senior-most police officer available.”</p>
<p>However, it provided guidelines for a phased use of force to disperse violent protesters. “When it is required to use force as per law, its application shall be of minimum essential standard,” it stated.</p>
<p>The guidelines allowed the use of force to be graduated from the minimum to the “optimum level required” in the following manner:</p>
<ul>
<li>In the first phase, the violent protesters may clearly be warned against violence before starting use of force. If the need arises after warning them, tear gas shells/grenades shall be used at a safe distance to disperse them</li>
<li>Rubber bullet guns and paper ball guns can be used against violent protesters from a safe distance to disperse them</li>
<li>In the second phase, if the situation requires, violent protesters may be “stopped with baton charge by using the anti-riot gear”. The special unarmed squad will be activated to apprehend violent protesters and take appropriate legal action.</li>
<li>In case of extreme violence and imminent threat to life and property, and when the violent protesters resist dispersal, aerial firing can be conducted by the special armed personnel/squad only with the direction of the senior-most officer present at the occasion.</li>
</ul>
<p>The guidelines directed personnel to exercise “extreme caution” while using force against protesters to avert damage to life and property.</p>
<p>“Anti-riot squad or the personnel entrusted with use of force shall be properly equipped with anti-riot to avoid damage/casualties to life of all concerned.”</p>
<p>Station house officers (SHOs) were also told to“arrange video-recording, preferably through professional cameramen, of the entire protest/procession”.</p>
<p>The police were directed to seize firearm weapons or any article referred to in Section 86, Sub-Section (1) of the KP Police Act from any person possessing them and take legal action against the individual.</p>
<p>The guidelines issued by the IG said district police officers (DPOs), sub-divisional police officers (SDPOs) and SHOs were to personally attend to all protests in their areas of jurisdiction.</p>
<p>To prevent “unlawful assemblies”, any police officer could temporarily close or regulate any street or public place to prohibit persons or vehicles from entering the area for security reasons under Section 88 of the KP Police Act, 2017.</p>
<p>To prevent “serious disorder, breach of the law or imminent danger to life and property, appropriate use of force will be ordered” by the sub-divisional police officers (SDPOs), SHOs, or the senior-most officer present at the site.</p>
<p>The police strength shall include the following formations:</p>
<ul>
<li>Anti-riot squad, fully equipped with anti-riot gear and sufficient amount of gas guns and gas shells, properly checked and verified for use by the reserve inspectors/moharrars</li>
<li>Special squads of unarmed men for the purpose of identifying and apprehending miscreants and violent protesters</li>
<li>Plain clothes personnel spread widely to identify and point out violent protesters, miscreants and saboteurs</li>
<li>Armed personnel shall only be deployed at important/suitable points in extremely urgent situations, only for public safety and security under the direct command of DPOs.</li>
</ul>
<p>SHOs were to specifically ensure deployment of sufficient police strength at vulnerable places, including police stations, government buildings, petrol stations, banks, shopping centres, and major highways and roads.</p>
<p>Police officers were also allowed to stop any procession which violates the conditions of a licence granted under section 84 of the KP Police Act and order it to disperse.</p>
<p>Shortly after the guidelines were issued, the KP information minister alleged that provincial police had withdrawn the security assigned to him and all parliamentarians.</p>
<p>“If any harm comes to me or any parliamentarian, the KP IG will be responsible,” he said.</p>

headline: CM Afridi says will not accept 'illegal move' of governor's rule or emergency in KP
description: PTI long march visits Mardan on its 7th day; IG issues guidelines for police to deal with protests; containers shifted to Swabi interchange but M-1, GT Road remain open.
author: Muhammad Jamal Hoti, Faiz Muhammad, Muqaddam Khan
article_text:
CHARSADDA/MARDAN: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Saturday said he will not accept any “illegal move”, including the imposition of governor’s rule or an emergency.

The KP CM made the remarks while addressing his supporters in Mardan, where the PTI long march led by him arrived on its seventh day. The federal government, citing differences over the counterterrorism policy, is mulling the option of imposing an emergency or governor’s rule in KP.

Afridi said that if governor’s rule was imposed or any “wrong decision” was taken, the long march would head to Peshawar instead of Swabi, and then move towards D-Chowk in Islamabad.

He urged the public to come out for the release of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, adding that Pakhtuns would not be intimidated by threats, guns or bullets.

The KP CM asserted that arrests and other measures could not demoralise PTI workers. He said that his party would continue its struggle to end the injustices being committed against Imran and secure his release.

Speaking on the occasion, MNA Muhammad Atif Khan contended that Afridi had placed the federal government in a difficult position through his strategy.

The PTI launched the march despite warnings from the Centre after Oct 3 talks with the federal government failed to bridge their differences for multiple reasons, particularly over counterterrorism measures.

The route plan for the march has undergone multiple changes since its launch on Oct 4. While the party initially vowed to march towards Islamabad, its final destination seemingly remains tentative as the KP CM has yet to announce the plan for the trek after Oct 11, beyond Swabi.

So far, the march — being carried out to demand Imran’s release — has remained within KP, where the PTI is in power.

Swabi authorities prepare for PTI march

Meanwhile, containers have been transported to Swabi Interchange and the Indus River bridge on the M-1 Motorway to block the party’s march, but the motorway and the Grand Trunk Road remain open to traffic.

The bridge is particularly significant because it links Punjab and KP, which lie on opposite banks of the river.

Afridi earlier called on PTI supporters across Pakistan to reach the Swabi Interchange on Oct 11 to join his long march.

However, PTI district president Sohail Yousafzai said the convoy would reach Swabi on Oct 12 (Monday), adding that Afridi had directed party workers, lawmakers and office-bearers from across the country to reach Swabi by then.

Echoing a plan announced by Afridi earlier, Yousafzai said that convoys from the Peshawar, Malakand and Kohat regions would reach Swabi Interchange on Oct 13, while those from Hazara, Bannu and Dera Ismail Khan would arrive the next day, when the CM Afridi would announce the next course of action.

The KP chief executive is expected to address party workers at Shewa Adda in Razaar tehsil at 1pm, at the district headquarters at 3pm and at Topi tehsil at 5pm, which shares a boundary with Ghazi in Haripur district.

In a post on X earlier in the day, KP Information Minister Shafi Jan said the convoy will stay overnight in Mardan. He also said the future course of action will be announced on Oct 13 and they will move beyond Swabi.

Refused pressure, Afridi claims

Earlier in the day, the KP CM addressed a large gathering at Farooq-i-Azam Chowk in Charsadda, where he reiterated his opposition to any military operations in the province.

Afridi said he stood firmly with the people and would not accept decisions imposed through pressure or threats.

“I was asked to sign, but I refused,” he said, adding that he would neither retreat from his position under pressure nor compromise on his principles.

Afridi said his position on national security and the Kashmir issue was clear and unequivocal. He noted that important national matters should be addressed on the basis of principles rather than political pressure.

Referring to what he alleged were preparations for a possible military operation, the KP CM reiterated that he would not sign any document under pressure. He claimed attempts had been made to persuade him to agree to certain decisions, but he had declined.

Afridi has repeatedly voiced his opposition to the federal government’s policies on counterterrorism and Afghanistan since he was elected as the KP chief minister in October 2025.

Speaking in Charsadda, the PTI leader stressed the need to protect public rights, democratic values and the people’s mandate, saying public aspirations and ground realities should not be ignored in decision-making. He urged party workers to remain united and maintain discipline in their political struggle.

He referred to the “threats” of the imposition of governor’s rule or emergency, adding that the matter “had gone beyond seats and power” and he was ready to “sacrifice” his seat for Imran and Pakhtuns.

The chief minister highlighted that KP had suffered immense losses in the fight against terrorism, adding that the sacrifices made by its residents should not be forgotten and that their concerns regarding peace, stability and fundamental rights deserved serious attention.

Afridi reiterated he would announce the next plan of action on Oct 13 at the Swabi interchange.

He called on PTI workers to remain united in their struggle for their rights, adding that political differences should be resolved through democratic means and that the voice of the people should be respected.

The KP CM urged party supporters to remain steadfast and vigilant amid the prevailing political situation.

The gathering drew hundreds of PTI supporters to the roundabout, many wearing red caps and chanting slogans in support of Imran. The chief minister addressed the crowd from a container alongside party leaders.

Guidelines issued for police to deal with protests

While the PTI seemed determined to continue with its long march, KP Inspector General Zulfiqar Hameed issued operational guidelines to the police to deal with protests.

The document issued by the police chief, available with Dawn, noted that in “all cases of public protests there is a possibility that miscreants and anti-state elements may use an opportunity to [incite] violence and carry out sabotage activities”.

To prevent such acts, the guidelines were issued in continuation of Operational Guidelines-9/2013 and in light of Sections 83 to 88 of the KP Police Act 2017, for “strict compliance”.

The KP IG directed personnel to exercise “maximum restraint” and avoid the use of force for peaceful protests. “The protesters shall be engaged in negotiations through the senior-most police officer available.”

However, it provided guidelines for a phased use of force to disperse violent protesters. “When it is required to use force as per law, its application shall be of minimum essential standard,” it stated.

The guidelines allowed the use of force to be graduated from the minimum to the “optimum level required” in the following manner:

In the first phase, the violent protesters may clearly be warned against violence before starting use of force. If the need arises after warning them, tear gas shells/grenades shall be used at a safe distance to disperse them
Rubber bullet guns and paper ball guns can be used against violent protesters from a safe distance to disperse them
In the second phase, if the situation requires, violent protesters may be “stopped with baton charge by using the anti-riot gear”. The special unarmed squad will be activated to apprehend violent protesters and take appropriate legal action.
In case of extreme violence and imminent threat to life and property, and when the violent protesters resist dispersal, aerial firing can be conducted by the special armed personnel/squad only with the direction of the senior-most officer present at the occasion.

The guidelines directed personnel to exercise “extreme caution” while using force against protesters to avert damage to life and property.

“Anti-riot squad or the personnel entrusted with use of force shall be properly equipped with anti-riot to avoid damage/casualties to life of all concerned.”

Station house officers (SHOs) were also told to“arrange video-recording, preferably through professional cameramen, of the entire protest/procession”.

The police were directed to seize firearm weapons or any article referred to in Section 86, Sub-Section (1) of the KP Police Act from any person possessing them and take legal action against the individual.

The guidelines issued by the IG said district police officers (DPOs), sub-divisional police officers (SDPOs) and SHOs were to personally attend to all protests in their areas of jurisdiction.

To prevent “unlawful assemblies”, any police officer could temporarily close or regulate any street or public place to prohibit persons or vehicles from entering the area for security reasons under Section 88 of the KP Police Act, 2017.

To prevent “serious disorder, breach of the law or imminent danger to life and property, appropriate use of force will be ordered” by the sub-divisional police officers (SDPOs), SHOs, or the senior-most officer present at the site.

The police strength shall include the following formations:

Anti-riot squad, fully equipped with anti-riot gear and sufficient amount of gas guns and gas shells, properly checked and verified for use by the reserve inspectors/moharrars
Special squads of unarmed men for the purpose of identifying and apprehending miscreants and violent protesters
Plain clothes personnel spread widely to identify and point out violent protesters, miscreants and saboteurs
Armed personnel shall only be deployed at important/suitable points in extremely urgent situations, only for public safety and security under the direct command of DPOs.

SHOs were to specifically ensure deployment of sufficient police strength at vulnerable places, including police stations, government buildings, petrol stations, banks, shopping centres, and major highways and roads.

Police officers were also allowed to stop any procession which violates the conditions of a licence granted under section 84 of the KP Police Act and order it to disperse.

Shortly after the guidelines were issued, the KP information minister alleged that provincial police had withdrawn the security assigned to him and all parliamentarians.

“If any harm comes to me or any parliamentarian, the KP IG will be responsible,” he said.

To prevent such acts, the guidelines were issued in continuation of Operational Guidelines-9/2013 and in light of Sections 83 to 88 of the KP Police Act 2017, for “strict compliance”.

The KP IG directed personnel to exercise “maximum restraint” and avoid the use of force for peaceful protests. “The protesters shall be engaged in negotiations through the senior-most police officer available.”

The guidelines allowed the use of force to be graduated from the minimum to the “optimum level required” in the following manner:

  • In the second phase, if the situation requires, violent protesters may be “stopped with baton charge by using the anti-riot gear”. The special unarmed squad will be activated to apprehend violent protesters and take appropriate legal action.

The police strength shall include the following formations:

  • Anti-riot squad, fully equipped with anti-riot gear and sufficient amount of gas guns and gas shells, properly checked and verified for use by the reserve inspectors/moharrars
  • Special squads of unarmed men for the purpose of identifying and apprehending miscreants and violent protesters
  • Plain clothes personnel spread widely to identify and point out violent protesters, miscreants and saboteurs
  • Armed personnel shall only be deployed at important/suitable points in extremely urgent situations, only for public safety and security under the direct command of DPOs.

SHOs were to specifically ensure deployment of sufficient police strength at vulnerable places, including police stations, government buildings, petrol stations, banks, shopping centres, and major highways and roads.

Police officers were also allowed to stop any procession which violates the conditions of a licence granted under section 84 of the KP Police Act and order it to disperse.

    <div dir='auto' class='story__content  flow-root    pt-1 mt-1 text-4 sm:text-4.5  overflow-visible'><p>The Rawalpindi deputy commissioner on Saturday announced that Section 144 had been imposed in the district for a period of 30 days, over threats to sensitive installations and other critical infrastructure.</p>
<p>Section 144 is a provision in the Code of Criminal Procedure which empowers local authorities to ban public gatherings such as rallies, processions and sit-ins, as well as the open display of weapons.</p>
<p>It has been imposed amid the PTI’s <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2034698">long march</a>, which has so far remained within Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, but had initially announced to move towards the federal capital. The KP chief minister reiterated today that he would lead the convoy towards Islamabad.</p>
<p>According to a notification seen by <em>Dawn</em>, the District Intelligence Committee (DIC) in a meeting today warned the DC of an “imminent threat” within the district to sensitive installations, major roads and other infrastructure “which may pose a serious risk to human life, public property, and the overall peace and order of the district”.</p>
<p>“The DIC has reported specific intelligence suggesting that certain groups and elements are actively mobilising with intentions to disturb the law and order situation through large gatherings, protests, and disruptive assemblies,” the notification read.</p>
    <figure class='media  w-full  w-full  media--  media--embed  media--uneven media--tweet' data-original-src='https://x.com/DCRawalpindi/status/2108961831419347128'>
        <div class='media__item  media__item--twitter  '><span>
    <blockquote class="twitter-tweet" lang="en">
        <a href="https://twitter.com/DCRawalpindi/status/2108961831419347128"></a>
    </blockquote>
</span></div>
        
    </figure>
<p>Moreover, the committee indicated that these elements may mobilise “individuals with the potential to engage in violent actions” against soft targets and near key installations and other sensitive sites.</p>
<p>Imposing Section 144, DC retired Captain Nadeem Nasir prohibited public gatherings of more than five people, as well as the open display of weapons, improvised explosives, spikes, laden batons, gulails, ball bearings, petrol bombs,  or other instruments that could cause physical harm.</p>
<p>It also banned the use of drones and any attempts to “remove any restriction” imposed by the police to regulate assemblies and traffic.</p>
<p>The order is set to expire on Nov 8.</p>
<p>Section 144 has already been imposed in several parts of the country, with Islamabad <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2032130">imposing the provision</a> for two months in a notification dated September 18.</p>
<p>The order prohibited gatherings of five or more people, as well as processions, rallies and demonstrations, at any public place within the revenue limits of the district, including the Red Zone.</p>
<p>Similarly, Section 144 is <a href="https://www.dawn.com/news/2035288">in force</a> in Lahore until Oct 15, with the order citing serious threats to public peace, tranquillity and the safety of life and property.</p>
<p>According to a notification issued by the Punjab Home Department, a complete ban was imposed on assemblies, processions and gatherings of five or more persons at public places, roads and open spaces.</p>
<p>However, the ban would not apply to wedding ceremonies, funeral prayers, burials, mosques and other places of worship, courts or government institutions.</p>

headline: Section 144 imposed in Rawalpindi district for a month over 'threat to law and order'
description: Ban on public gatherings, display of weapons in effect until Nov 8; notification notes groups "actively mobilising" to disrupt law and order.
author: News Desk
article_text:
The Rawalpindi deputy commissioner on Saturday announced that Section 144 had been imposed in the district for a period of 30 days, over threats to sensitive installations and other critical infrastructure.

Section 144 is a provision in the Code of Criminal Procedure which empowers local authorities to ban public gatherings such as rallies, processions and sit-ins, as well as the open display of weapons.

It has been imposed amid the PTI’s long march, which has so far remained within Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, but had initially announced to move towards the federal capital. The KP chief minister reiterated today that he would lead the convoy towards Islamabad.

According to a notification seen by Dawn, the District Intelligence Committee (DIC) in a meeting today warned the DC of an “imminent threat” within the district to sensitive installations, major roads and other infrastructure “which may pose a serious risk to human life, public property, and the overall peace and order of the district”.

“The DIC has reported specific intelligence suggesting that certain groups and elements are actively mobilising with intentions to disturb the law and order situation through large gatherings, protests, and disruptive assemblies,” the notification read.

Moreover, the committee indicated that these elements may mobilise “individuals with the potential to engage in violent actions” against soft targets and near key installations and other sensitive sites.

Imposing Section 144, DC retired Captain Nadeem Nasir prohibited public gatherings of more than five people, as well as the open display of weapons, improvised explosives, spikes, laden batons, gulails, ball bearings, petrol bombs, or other instruments that could cause physical harm.

It also banned the use of drones and any attempts to “remove any restriction” imposed by the police to regulate assemblies and traffic.

The order is set to expire on Nov 8.

Section 144 has already been imposed in several parts of the country, with Islamabad imposing the provision for two months in a notification dated September 18.

The order prohibited gatherings of five or more people, as well as processions, rallies and demonstrations, at any public place within the revenue limits of the district, including the Red Zone.

Similarly, Section 144 is in force in Lahore until Oct 15, with the order citing serious threats to public peace, tranquillity and the safety of life and property.

According to a notification issued by the Punjab Home Department, a complete ban was imposed on assemblies, processions and gatherings of five or more persons at public places, roads and open spaces.

However, the ban would not apply to wedding ceremonies, funeral prayers, burials, mosques and other places of worship, courts or government institutions.
